E1.title: Rank-aware TopKTrades order check; notional cell construction
E1.ruling: No other shared-validator change is made in EF4. The shared `TopKTrades` order check becomes rank-aware (a ranking-aware order check or a ranking field) in a later change before any layer relies on the notional cell through the public constructor. Until then the pinned workaround stands: `tape.top_k_notional` cells are assembled with `object.__new__(TopKTrades)` plus `object.__setattr__`; the io codec reads a stored cell feature-aware (only `tape.top_k_notional` is notional-ordered); the bundles decoder still refuses notional cells.
contract_lines: TAPE_CONTRACT_PROPOSAL.md DP-K4 (line 190) and OQ-6 (line 209): the cell, its Arrow struct and the registry type stay unchanged
TAPE_CONTRACT_PROPOSAL.md line 78 and DP-K2 (line 188): rank key (-notional, event_ns, order_key, event_id)
fixture TK01 (rank d, a, c against the size order e, b, d)

merged_behavior.library: `notional_cell` (ef4/_tape_topk.py:62) first validates the rows with the shared constructor in the size order (types, bounds, duplicates, K), then builds the frozen cell in the notional order with `object.__new__` and `object.__setattr__`. It is used by `compute_trade_top_k_notional` and `merge_trade_top_k_notional`. The shared `TopKTrades.__post_init__` (packages/contracts results.py:211) is unchanged and still demands the size-ranked key, so `dataclasses.replace(cell)`, `TopKTrades(k, rows)` on notional-ordered rows or any restore that revalidates raises `INVALID_ORDER`. The rank-aware check itself is NOT implemented anywhere; it is the amendment item.
merged_behavior.io: equity-feature-io main 4ebfa30, io-sdk codec.py: `_decode` decodes the `feature_id` of a `FeatureColumn` first and passes `notional = (feature == 'tape.top_k_notional')` down; only then `_notional_cell` assembles the cell: k bound 1..10000, row types, duplicate (input_id, event_id) identity, AND the rows must follow the notional rank (-price*size, event_ns, order_key, event_id), else `SinkError INVALID_CONTENT`; then `object.__new__`. Every other feature keeps the shared constructor and its size order. Bundles (packages/bundles `_typed.py`) rebuild `r.TopKTrades(k=..., rows=...)` through the public constructor, so a notional cell is refused there.

E2.title: Coverage form and the fail-open of undeclared coverage
E2.ruling: The declaration is one `IntervalCoverage` entry exactly equal to [S, E) on the quote or trade batch, with the aggregate `Coverage` as fallback (complete; incomplete with a known `expected`; undeclared when `expected` is null). Bars use per-slot entries equal to a grid slot. An undeclared batch that delivers rows is read as complete: this fails open, so every I/O mapper must always declare coverage; the tape adapter does not enforce this (it defaults to complete, see the I/O line).
contract_lines: QUOTE_VWAP_CONTRACT_PROPOSAL.md line 85 (DP-Q3, DP-Q11): delivery completeness is the declared IntervalCoverage
PATH_EFFICIENCY_CONTRACT_PROPOSAL.md line 46 and PATH_PROJECTIONS (per-slot coverage names `bar:<i>`, `slot:<i>`)

merged_behavior.library: `declared_coverage` (ef4/_common.py:200): any interval entry must be exactly one entry equal to [S, E) with observed equal to the delivered rows, else `INCONSISTENT_IDENTITY`; with no entry the aggregate is read: complete is complete, incomplete with `expected` not null is incomplete, incomplete with `expected` null is `undeclared`. Zero rows with `undeclared` (or an undelivered role) is `absent_input` (_quote.py:170, _vwap.py:149). `undeclared` with rows is not gated as incomplete, so it reads as complete. Bars (VWAP bar source): a per-slot entry must equal a grid slot; no row with an entry is `governed_gap`, no row without one is `absent_input`, a delivered row whose entry is incomplete is `governed_gap` (implementation document; no fixture). Path efficiency and the projections declare per slot and treat a slot without a coverage entry as absent.
merged_behavior.io: Adapter sources read (io main 4ebfa30). Quote/VWAP `quote_vwap.py` `_event_coverage` (line 158): coverage must be declared complete, incomplete or absent (else INVALID_CONFIG); absent with delivered rows is refused; every declared batch carries the aggregate and one interval entry for the scope. Projections `ef4_projections.py` declares the aggregate on every batch (line 170) plus per-slot entries (lines 205-257). Path efficiency `path_efficiency.py` writes the aggregate `Coverage(None, n, False)` (line 126) and relies on the per-slot entries (lines 113-119). Tape `tape.py:136` DEFAULTS to `Coverage(n, n, True)` when the caller supplies none: a fail-open default (a tape batch delivered without a declaration is declared complete by the adapter).
merged_behavior.workers: Not specific; the workers pass the adapter batches through.

E4.title: governed_history is capped at N <= 63 and uses the R17 carry context
E4.ruling: `epoch_profile = governed_history` requires an R17 context in `carry` mode (anchor at the start of the supplied daily grid; no value crosses a session boundary); `session_reset` requires `reset`. The R17 context holds at most 64 sessions and `governed_history` has one governed slot per session, so N is capped at 63 daily returns per context. The cap is a coordinator decision; no code split is made.
contract_lines: PATH_EFFICIENCY_CONTRACT_PROPOSAL.md line 22: window N 2..4096, epoch_profile session_reset | governed_history
PATH_EFFICIENCY_CONTRACT_PROPOSAL.md line 46 (bars role, R17 chunked delivery) and line 70 (epoch, DP-E3, line 123: no carry)

merged_behavior.library: `_path_config.py`: `_MODE = {session_reset: reset, governed_history: carry}`; an `epoch_profile` that disagrees with the context mode, or the profile value `carry` itself, is `INVALID_CONFIG` (lines 38 and 64); a `carry` context whose slot count differs from its session count is `INVALID_CONFIG` (line 66). `_context.py` (line 82) bounds a context at 1..64 sessions, which gives N + 1 <= 64 slots, N <= 63. There is no explicit `window <= 63` check: `window` keeps the range 2..4096 and a window beyond the delivered slots gives `insufficient_history` at compute (window 4096 is a valid config whose result is always `insufficient_history`; 4095 is the largest session_reset window that can be available).
merged_behavior.io: Not specific to the cap (the I1 I/O record builds the context and config with the adapter and compares the envelope to `build_path_efficiency_config`).

E8.title: Top-K merge worker uses one shared configuration
E8.ruling: A merge task has one reviewed configuration for all partitions. The worker computes one partial per leaf with the library top-K producer and merges along the role tree with `merge_trade_top_k_notional`. Nine refusal recipes therefore have no worker path and are checked at the library only: RF41, RF42, RF43, RF54, RF55, RF60, RF65, RF66 and RF69.
